title: k8s node lifecycle debugging scratchpad - post-provision NotReady
content:
Context:
- New batch of spot nodes being provisioned for dedicated pool (gke/custom-instance templates). Several nodes come up in Ready briefly then flip to NotReady within ~3-7 minutes.
- Symptoms observed: kubelet logs show repeated errors about container runtime sandbox creation + image pull backoff on system pods (kube-proxy, calico-node). Some nodes show kernel OOM kills on containerd.

What I saw (commands & excerpts):
1) node status
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide
NAME                                STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP    EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE
np-spot-12-7d8f                      NotReady   <none>   6m    v1.25.6   10.140.0.12    -             Ubuntu 20.04
np-spot-12-b4c3                      Ready      <none>   8m    v1.25.6   10.140.0.13    -             Ubuntu 20.04

2) kubelet journal (np-spot-12-7d8f):
$ journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
Mar 01 12:12:07 np-spot-12-7d8f kubelet[1234]: E0301 12:12:07.123456    1234 pod_workers.go:191] "Failed to create pod sandbox: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to create containerd task: failed to create shim: OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: error running hook #0: error running hook: exit status 1, stdout: '', stderr: 'failed to setrlimit: cannot allocate memory'"
Mar 01 12:12:08 np-spot-12-7d8f kubelet[1234]: W0301 12:12:08.000000    1234 kubelet.go:2200] Failed creating pod infra for pod kube-system/kube-proxy-abcde: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start containerd task

3) dmesg / kernel logs (same node):
[    25.123456] Out of memory: Kill process 2345 (containerd) score 987 or sacrifice child
[    25.123459] Killed process 2345 (containerd) total-vm:2783916kB, anon-rss:1857120kB

4) containerd info/checks:
$ sudo systemctl status containerd● containerd.service - containerd
   Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/containerd.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
   Active: active (running) since Sun 2026-02-25 12:10:01; 6min ago
$ sudo crictl ps -a
CONTAINER           IMAGE               CREATED              STATE               POD
(many crashes / short lived)

5) kube-proxy + calico failing to start: image pull backoff on calico-node pod on many NotReady nodes.

Commands tried so far (notes & outcomes):
- Reprovisioned one node (restarted VM) -> node came Ready for ~4m then NotReady again. Pattern reproduced.
- Checked instance template: boot disk size correct, kubelet flags in systemd unit match cluster (--cgroup-driver=systemd). No obvious mismatch.
- Compared sysctl between healthy and unhealthy nodes: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max set to 131072 on both. No difference.
- Increased systemd service memory limit? (tried editing /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/20-extra.conf to set LimitNOFILE/LimitNPROC) -> didn't change behavior.
- Disabled swap (confirmed off).
- kubelet --v=4 logs show repeated errors: "failed to find available memory for sandbox" and runc complaining about RLIMIT_NPROC/NOFILE maybe too low.
- Looked at cloud-init script: heavy image pulls at boot for sidecar + infra pods could be causing memory spike during startup (ephemeral nodes try to pull large model-serving images from our private registry).
- Temporarily added node taint to avoid scheduling heavy pods: nodes stayed Ready longer but when image pulls started, memory pressure returned.

Hypotheses / root cause suspects:
1) Boot-time memory contention: startup-script is pulling large images (model-serving) and CNI + kube-proxy + kube-system pods all start concurrently, causing containerd memory usage spike and OOM kills.
2) Instance type autoscaler selection: cheap spot instance has smaller memory than expected due to custom machine-type mismatch in instance template (e.g., template says n1-highmem-4 but actual instance created as n1-standard-2) -> can verify metadata on GCE console and compare flavors.
3) Kernel / container runtime limits: RLIMITs too low for runc when many containers start; but default should be fine — less likely.
4) CNI (calico) version incompatible with kernel/iptables mode causing crash loops -> exacerbates scheduling of other pods.
5) Image pull throughput/registry throttling -> long pull times cause many containers to be in creation state and increase memory use.

Short experiments to run next (ordered):
- Verify actual machine type and memory on one failing instance: curl GCE metadata (or gcloud compute instances describe) -> confirm machine type & memory.
- Boot with a lighter startup-script (disable model-serving base image pulls) to see if nodes stay Ready. Use imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent for our heavy images? Hard at cluster level but can test by removing taints on a single test node with scaled-down DaemonSet.
- Add forced kubelet --eviction-hard thresholds (memory.available<200Mi) to proactively evict rather than OOM-kill containerd — but risk of pod churn.
- Temporarily change node pool autoscaler to use larger machine type for new nodes.
- Inspect registry metrics for throttling/errors (private registry helm chart, GH-PR-4892 mentions recent credential rotation).

Useful commands to run quickly:
- gcloud compute instances describe np-spot-12-7d8f --zone=us-central1-a --format='value(machineType,zone)'
- ssh into node and run: free -m; sudo cat /proc/meminfo; ps aux --sort=-rss | head -n 20; sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200
- kubectl describe pod -n kube-system calico-node-xxxxx
- crictl inspectp <pod-infra-pid> / crictl stats

Notes / breadcrumbs for follow-up:
- Slack thread: #infra -> link: slack://channel/infra/thread/CK3... (see messages around Feb 25)
- Related JIRA: JIRA-4521 (node pool unstable after credential rotation)
- PR that rotated registry creds: GH-PR-4892 (may have introduced transient 401s causing retries and extra memory pressure)
- Confluence: infra/k8s-node-provisioning-notes (contains recent changes to instance templates and startup scripts).

Immediate mitigation applied (temporary):
- Added a cluster-level PDB and scaled down model-serving deployments in staging pool. Marked new node pool with larger machine type for further nodes.

Longer-term actions to consider:
- Change startup ordering: delay non-critical DaemonSet images (model-serving pulls) until after CNI and kube-proxy stabilize. For example, use init containers or startupProbe + imagePullPolicy tweaks.
- Add pre-pulled base images to instance image cache (pre-bake AMI/GCE image) to avoid large pulls at boot.
- Harden container runtime OOM behaviour by tuning eviction thresholds and containerd configs.
- Add more observability on containerd memory usage via Node exporter / cAdvisor metrics during bootstrap.

TODOs (who/when):
- [ ] Jordan: run machine type verification + try repro with disabled startup pulls (today)
- [ ] Emily: check registry logs and rate limits + verify recent credential rotation (ASAP)
- [ ] Sam: propose instance template change to enforce min machine type (tomorrow)

Scratch notes: keep this doc as breadcrumbs for incident postmortem. If we confirm registry rotation + heavy image pulls are the root cause, link to rollout plan for credential rollback and baked image creation.

End of scratchpad.
